strings.name: Rem Koolhaas
strings.role: Architect and theorist · Urban life and architectural research
strings.summary: Koolhaas moved from journalism and screenwriting into architecture. OMA’s designs and AMO’s research examine urban life, institutions and globalization. Delirious New York reinterprets Manhattan; S,M,L,XL turns a practice’s projects into experiments with theory and images. Buildings such as Seattle Central Library and CCTV headquarters reorganize programs and circulation. The 2000 Pritzker laureate also works through education, exhibitions and research on rural territories.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1944–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Reconsidered urban life through architectural design and theoretical writing including Delirious New York, influencing international architectural education and urban studies.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education and early work
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Worked as a journalist and screenwriter; graduated from the Architectural Association in London in 1972
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Architecture and theory develop together
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Delirious New York and S,M,L,XL combine urban observation, projects and visual organization, influencing architectural debate and education.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Reorganizing civic programs
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Seattle Central Library’s Books Spiral and layered public spaces respond to growing collections and the circulation of knowledge across media.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Reflects on fifty years of OMA
strings.timeline.event-01.text: At the Berlage in Delft he discussed place, design methods and choices about working in different political settings with a critic and students.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: New Museum expansion opens in New York
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The OMA project co-led with Shohei Shigematsu added galleries, circulation and public facilities beside the original SANAA building.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Curates Countryside, The Future
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The Guggenheim exhibition turned to nonurban territories, examining how technology, ecology and political forces transform rural space.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: CCTV headquarters is completed
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Developed with Ole Scheeren and the wider team, a continuous loop organizes television production and administration, departing from the conventional tower.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Seattle Central Library opens
strings.timeline.event-05.text: With Joshua Prince-Ramus and collaborators, the Books Spiral and layered platforms reorganized books, activities and civic space.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Receives the Pritzker Architecture Prize
strings.timeline.event-06.text: The award recognized a practice joining design and ideas, bringing international recognition to exchanges between buildings, writing and research.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Publishes S,M,L,XL
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Created with graphic designer Bruce Mau, the book organizes material by project size and juxtaposes architecture, theory, fiction and observation.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Publishes Delirious New York
strings.timeline.event-08.text: A retroactive manifesto interprets Manhattan’s density and culture, establishing a major foundation for his urban research and architectural theory.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Co-founds OMA
strings.timeline.event-09.text: With Madelon Vriesendorp and Elia and Zoe Zenghelis, he established a practice translating writing and research into design.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Rotterdam
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in the Netherlands, he spent part of childhood in Indonesia and later moved from journalism and screenwriting into architectural study.
